extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, newsroom product people, and news-interested readers interested in editorial curation and judgment
extracted.subtask_description: A short, practice-focused rubric for deciding what stories deserve attention in an algorithmically amplified media environment; aimed at helping curators and editors resist virality-driven selection. Emphasizes tests and heuristics for distinguishing durable, consequential reporting from ephemeral, platform-driven noise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signal vs. noise
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the story tell us something durable or is it ephemeral discourse foam?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer coverage that conveys lasting informational value rather than transient, attention-seeking pieces. Be skeptical of items that exist mainly to generate conversation without adding substantive facts or context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-world stakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Not just 'online' stakes — what happens off-platform?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize stories with tangible offline consequences (policy effects, legal outcomes, physical safety, economic impact) over stories whose impact remains purely on social platforms. Ask whether the piece matters beyond the feed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information vs. content
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there new information, or just commentary on commentary?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give precedence to reporting that produces new facts, documents, or verified claims. Deprioritize meta-commentary, reaction pieces, and iterative takes that don't advance the underlying reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asymmetry of consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Small online events with large offline impact get prioritized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify situations where seemingly minor or niche online activity yields disproportionate real-world consequences; such asymmetries merit attention because they reveal power or harm hidden by scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufactured vs. organic virality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate whether amplification is organic or the result of coordinated campaigns, PR stunts, bots, or platform manipulation. Treat engineered virality with skepticism and avoid amplifying manufactured agendas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on trending topics (X/TikTok)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trending topics on X / TikTok (often manipulated) should not by themselves drive front-page attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid elevating stories solely because they're trending on major platforms; verify substance and independence from manipulation before treating trending status as newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid outrage cycles without underlying news
rubrics_metrics.description: Outrage cycles that lack underlying factual developments should not drive coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist covering items that generate emotion but add no new reporting; such cycles often amplify harm and produce little journalistic value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't follow 'everyone's talking about it' (audience-generated agenda)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Everyone's talking about it' — audience-generated agenda — is not a sufficient reason to prioritize a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial judgment should not be outsourced to the crowd. Evaluate whether popular conversation corresponds to substantive developments before allocating attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid discourse-about-discourse
rubrics_metrics.description: Discourse about discourse (meta-discussion) should not be treated as news in its own right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of pieces that exist only to comment on previous commentary; prefer direct reporting over recursive analysis of online conversations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not treat tech executive proclamations as inherent news
rubrics_metrics.description: Tech executive proclamations are not automatically newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require verification, context, and demonstrable impact before amplifying claims or speeches from industry leaders. Distinguish marketing or opinion from reported developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid AI hype cycles disconnected from reality
rubrics_metrics.description: AI hype cycles disconnected from product reality should not drive attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinize AI-related stories for actual technical or product advances versus speculative hype. Avoid repeating buzzwords or speculative claims without corroborating evidence of real-world effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: The week-from-now test
rubrics_metrics.description: Will anyone remember this story in seven days?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this temporal durability test to filter ephemeral items. If the answer is likely 'no,' deprioritize unless there are exceptional reasons (e.g., immediate safety, breaking legal developments).

rubrics_metrics.name: The off-platform test
rubrics_metrics.description: Does this story exist outside the platform that surfaced it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the story is supported by reporting, documents, or consequences beyond the originating social platform. Stories that only live on-platform are more likely to be noise or manufactured.

rubrics_metrics.name: The new-information test
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there reporting, or just reaction?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask whether new facts, documents, or reporting are present. Favor pieces that add verifiable information rather than aggregating reactions or takes.

rubrics_metrics.name: The power-mapping test
rubrics_metrics.description: Who benefits if this becomes the story?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map incentives and beneficiaries to reveal conflicts, PR influence, or coordinated campaigns. If amplification primarily serves an actor's interests rather than public understanding, treat coverage with caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall anti-virality principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Good news judgment requires resisting platform-amplified salience; the rubric is essentially anti-virality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the above heuristics and tests collectively to avoid defaulting to virality as a proxy for importance. Editorial curation should privilege durable, consequential reporting over platform-driven attention.
